title: Status cannot do what nearness does.
summary: The shabad contrasts desire-driven reaching with being held close. One is hungry display. The other is actual relation.
lifeApplication: Trade one status reflex today for one act of quiet remembrance.

source.shortMeaning: The life that keeps reaching for riches is not the same life that learns nearness.
source.lifeApplication: The deepest correction may be relational, not performative.

evidence.coreClaim: The life that keeps reaching for riches is not the same life that learns nearness.
evidence.turn: Nearness is received in humility, not built out of status.
evidence.practicalImplication: Trade one status reflex today for one act of quiet remembrance.
